reference.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(x/2+y/3=1\)?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Read the intercept form

The denominator under \(y\) is the \(y\)-intercept, 3.

Method 2: Use the definition of the y-intercept

A point on the \(y\)-axis has \(x=0\). Substituting into the line equation gives \(y/3=1\), so \(y=3\). Thus the \(y\)-intercept is \(3\).
